subject: Celestia performance incident — peering/VPC path review and exec sync request
participants_external: Sara Holden <sara@celestia.com> (Head of Platform, Celestia Analytics)
messages:
From: Sara Holden <sara@celestia.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@celestia.com
Date: 2028-04-22T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: sustained latency spike + 5xx increase impacting checkout (need exec visibility)

Hi Marissa,

We're seeing a persistent latency spike and an uptick in 5xx errors for requests routed to Redwood in us-west-2 since ~06:30 PDT. Traffic volume is roughly normal but p95 tail has jumped from ~120ms to ~1.3s and 5xx rate climbed from 0.1% to ~3.8% for checkout traffic. This is causing lost conversions and our CEO is on the line asking for an exec-level rundown.

Initial customer-side triage shows:
- Multiple traceroutes with a hop at the peering handoff showing +200–400ms; occasional packet loss after the handoff.
- No config changes on our side.
- We see NAT session churn on our egress edge during bursts.

I've attached a sample traceroute and a KPI snapshot. Can Redwood confirm whether this looks like VPC peering degradation, DNS resolution issues, or a proxy/firewall queuing problem on your side? We need: a) a short technical summary we can use in our exec bridge, and b) a proposed remediation plan and ETA.

We appreciate rapid attention — please escalate internally as needed.

Thanks,
Sara Holden
Head of Platform, Celestia Analytics
(sara@celestia.com)

Attachment: celestia-peering-trace-20280422.txt (plain text)
Attachment: latency-kpi-snapshot-20280422.png

Subject: Re: Urgent: sustained latency spike + 5xx increase impacting checkout (need exec visibility)

Sara — thank you for the data and the heads-up. I'm escalating to our network and infra leads. Initial ask: can you confirm whether Celestia is using a pinned peering route or dynamic egress? That helps us reproduce.

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
- Vivek and Rafael will run end-to-end traceroutes and check our VPC peering telemetry and NAT pool health.
- We'll look at DNS resolution timelines (to rule out TTL expiry / stale records).
- If we confirm peering handoff latency, we'll propose a temporary routing fallback to an alternate peer while we triage.

We're standing up a short bridge at 09:00 PDT — I'll send invites and an exec-friendly one-slide summary within 30 min. If you have an internal exec bridge already, share the link and we'll join.

Marissa Cole

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-22T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sustained latency spike + 5xx increase impacting checkout (need exec visibility)

Quick technical findings from our side (first 40 minutes):

- Reproduced p95 jump to ~1.2s from our synthetic requests entering us-west-2.
- Traceroute to Celestia shows an asymmetric handoff at AS64512 -> AS32789 with per-hop latency increasing by ~320ms at the handoff. Attached is a consolidated traceroute.
- Our VPC peering telemetry (us-west-2 peer set A) shows elevated retransmits and a small but steady increase in connection establishment latency at the acceptor side. No spikes in CPU/memory on Redwood hosts.
- DNS lookups are stable; no rapid TTL churn observed.
- We observed NAT session backlog growth on Celestia-handshake prefixes — could be transient conns or NAT table exhaustion on their edge (they referenced NAT churn).

Preliminary hypothesis: latency and 5xx are caused by intermittent degradation at the peering handoff, with downstream NAT churn amplifying retries and creating request pile-up at the proxy layer. That fits the traceroute + NAT signs.

Immediate mitigations we can try now (we need Celestia sign-off for some):
1) Route failover: temporarily divert a percentage of traffic to a secondary peering path we control (low-risk config change on our edge).
2) Shorten keepalive timeout and increase circuit reclaim rate on Redwood proxies for Celestia prefixes to reduce queuing on transient bursts.
3) If NAT exhaustion is confirmed on Celestia's side, coordinate to increase ephemeral port pool or add SNAT proxies.

I'll be on the bridge at 09:00 PDT with traceroutes and a short playbook. Rafael — can you prepare a one-slide timeline and list of exactly-what-we-change (and rollback steps)?

— Vivek
Principal Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

Attachment: consolidated-traceroute-celestia-20280422.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Holden <sara@celestia.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, ops@celestia.com
Date: 2028-04-23T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Update and next steps — scheduled exec sync + temporary routing fallback

Sara — quick update following our investigation and the bridge this morning. Thanks for joining. Summary for your execs:

What we saw:
- Measured p95 increase and 5xx uplift correlated with latency introduced at an interconnect handoff between an intermediate AS and Celestia's ingress (~320ms added at the hop).
- Evidence of NAT session churn on Celestia prefixes (your team shared NAT counters on the bridge).
- DNS resolution did not contribute materially.

Action plan (agreed on bridge):
1) Immediate: Redwood will enact a temporary routing fallback for 25% of Celestia traffic to our secondary peer in us-west-2 to reduce exposure to the impacted handoff. This will be in place for up to 3 hours while we validate impact. (Rollback: 10 min change to revert routing).
2) Customer action: Celestia to increase ephemeral port pool and confirm SNAT proxy capacity (we'll coordinate change window).
3) Redwood infra change: shorten proxy keepalive for Celestia prefixes to accelerate circuit reclaim (no code deploy; infra config only).
4) Post-mortem: joint write-up within 48 hours; include timeline, root cause, and recommendations (longer-term peering changes).

We also prepared suggested exec wording (attached) should you need it for your CEO/board. We'll hold a short executive bridge today at 13:00 PDT to run through the above with both engineering and exec-level stakeholders — link below. If that time doesn't work, propose an alternate.

Exec bridge: https://meet.redwood.com/exec/2028-04-23-celestia-sync
Incident ticket: https://redwood.app/incident/INC-20280422-17

I'll remain the POC. Rafael and Vivek will monitor the rollback and report back. Thanks again for the partnership — we're prioritizing this and will follow up with the joint post-mortem.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
